correctness.rationale: The published complete parity-resolved Parikh spectrum gives j=#1 every integer in [p_n,q_n] and c=#0−#2 equal 0 when n−j even or both ±1 when odd. It also gives p_{4n−1}=n+p_n−1, q_{4n−1}=n+q_n, so q_{n_k}−p_{n_k}=k+1. For an allowed (j,c), total weight is ((a0+a2)n−Aj+Ec)/2. Equal weight requires AΔj=EΔc, with parity Δj≡Δc mod 2 and |Δc|≤2. If A≠0 and A∤E this forces Δj=Δc=0. If A=0, at most three weighted sums occur vs at least k+2 Parikh vectors. If A divides E, h=E/A, disjoint c=+1 at j versus c=−1 at j−2h pairs yield at least max(0,floor((k+2−2|h|)/2)) collisions, diverging. This is an actual infinite proof conditional on the published full-spectrum theorem; the finite verifier is not its replacement.

final_claim: For the infinite ternary Thue fixed point 0→012,1→02,2→1, a lengthwise integer valuation preserves all abelian factor classes for every length if and only if A=a0+a2−2a1≠0 and A does not divide E=a0−a2; otherwise the weighted/abelian complexity deficit grows without bound along n_k=(2·4^k+1)/3 with explicit k-dependent lower bounds.
